ledger.claim: The fare charges SGD 2.00 for the CTE (southbound) gantry after Braddell Road at 08:33, but this trip's own trace never goes near it: the closest of the 104 fixes, at 08:34:30, is 1,843.93 m from the gantry's recorded coordinates, and no fix lies anywhere within the 250 m radius that POL-RD-09(4) treats as a crossing. A charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure: it is refunded in full as a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4), available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a billing-integrity finding.

The SGD 2.00 has no counterpart on any account of this trip. The platform's own booking route itemised ERP of SGD 0.00, and the fare breakdown's ERP block records the charged gantry as not on the optimal route - SGD 2.00 off-optimal against SGD 0.00 on-optimal, with off_optimal_route_total of 2.00. Nothing in the bundle places the vehicle on the CTE, and the driver's own account on file is that he used Upper Thomson and never the CTE. The line is a phantom pass-through and falls squarely within POL-RD-09(4).

That absence of a CTE crossing cannot be written off as a data gap. The trace carries 104 fixes at a 10 s cadence from 08:21:50 to 08:38:57, with a largest interval of 10 s, no straight-line step above 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 s, so it is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); the vehicle's failure to approach the gantry is a real absence, not a hole in the record. The same trace is the governing distance measurement under POL-RD-01, and it is the trace figure that is used below.

On the trace figure that POL-RD-01 makes governing, the excess over the 8.7 km booked optimal is 1.14 km, or 13.1% of optimal - below the 20% establishment gate, so no route deviation is established, no POL-RD-02 recomputation of the distance and time lines runs, and the rider's '4-5 km extra' estimate is not made out. That finding does not empty the rider's case: POL-RD-01 expressly preserves a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) where neither establishment test is met, and it is on that limb - the SGD 2.00 CTE line charged for a gantry the trace never crosses - that the rider recovers on this trip.

The CTE line is refunded standalone and is not absorbed by any other limb: because no POL-RD-02 refund runs on this trip, POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule does not comprehend it, and POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out of its escalation trigger a charge line refunded under POL-RD-09(4). The case is therefore one that is decided with money moving on the disputed line, not one that escalates and leaves the amount held.

The governing measurement is the trace, not the rounded convenience copy: POL-RD-01 provides that gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs, and it is 9.84 km (EV-GPS-04006); trip_record.actual_distance_km of 9.8 km may NOT be cited for the threshold test. Optimal distance at booking is 8.7 km (EV-TRIP-04006). Excess is therefore 1.14 km, which is 13.10% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; the percentage limb fails outright, so no route deviation exists on this trip and the outcome on the distance and time charges is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the morning.

The rider's account - a loop round Yio Chu Kang, 'must be 4-5km extra', a fare that should have been 12-13 - is unsupported by any artifact in the bundle and is contradicted by the only measurement on file: 9.84 km driven against an 8.7 km optimal route, an excess of 1.14 km, roughly a quarter of what is asserted. The planned route itself (Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, Marymount Rd, Thomson Rd, Sinaran Dr) is the ordinary AMK-to-Novena corridor and matches the driver's statement that he took Upper Thomson and Thomson Road. Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden of showing an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, and the same clause provides that an assertion citing no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 104 fixes at a 10.0 s cadence from 08:21:50 to 08:38:57, no gap between consecutive fixes larger than 10 s, largest straight-line step 114.0 m, highest implied speed 41.0 km/h - every one of these is far inside the 90 s gap, 500 m jump and 30 s sustained-sampling limbs. The 1.14 km excess is therefore sound as measured, no independent corroboration is required of it, and POL-RD-10(3) has nothing to bite on.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory at all, and the artifact minted for it, EV-ADVIS-04006-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; per POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact can carry no fact and its absence is itself citable. Neither party cites that identifier or asserts an external traffic cause - the driver's statement is that he took the normal way, not that a road was closed - so under POL-RD-13 there is no assertion to test against it, POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable, and nothing in a missing advisory can supply an amended optimal route or a justified excess. Because no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact, this is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and it does not escalate the case under POL-RD-10(5).

On the one line the driver cannot defend, he does not try. The fare_breakdown carries a SGD 2.00 ERP line for the CTE (southbound) gantry after Braddell Road, at 1.3412, 103.8559, charged at 08:33:00; the nearest fix on the trace is 1,843.93 m away (index 76, 08:34:30) and no gap brackets a closest approach, so the vehicle never came within the 250 m match radius that POL-RD-09(4) applies. That is a standalone billing-integrity correction, refundable whether or not a deviation exists, and the driver's own counterparty statement says as much ('Never go CTE. The ERP charge not from me.'). It is a government pass-through that was never the driver's money; it is refunded as it stands, and it leaves the SGD 12.14 of distance and time charges (7.38 + 4.76) on this metered fare untouched.

POL-RD-02 is a remedy that runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'. No deviation is established here, so no recomputation is reached, the arithmetic of the optimal-route fare is never engaged, and no distance or time refund is available to the rider on the contested amount. In any event the metered lines are unimpeachable: 9.84 km at 0.75 per km and 17 min at 0.28 per min, with the surge multiplier of 1.0 read off fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, reconcile to the cent with the ledger and to the same trace that produced them.

The excess of 1.14 km at 13.10% is neither established nor material - materiality requires more than 50% of optimal or more than 8.0 km absolute - so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not triggered at all; and consulted anyway it returns the same answer: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 295, a ratio of 0.000 against a pattern threshold of 0.05. There is therefore no basis for a FULL_REFUND uplift on the remedy and no basis for a driver-conduct referral. The remaining profile fields (rating, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags, prior_disputes_filed) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not ground any finding.

ledger.claim: No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so this case must be ruled and not held. Trip identifier TRP-04006 matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown; the timestamps are causally ordered and the trace's first and last fixes equal started_at and ended_at to the second (08:21:50, 08:38:57); the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); no exculpatory clause is invoked against any cited artifact; the identifiers on the three artifacts agree; any refund computable on these figures is a small fraction of the SGD 18.74 charged and nowhere near the SGD 150.00 ceiling or the charged total; and the only unmatched charge line in the fare_breakdown is the ERP line dealt with under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts.

The outcome the driver seeks is NO_ACTION on the rider's contested amount. The rider filed; payment_status on the fare_breakdown is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and leaves the present payment state exactly as it stands - it never restores a charge and never converts an unsupported claim into a payout. The only movement the record supports is the SGD 2.00 pass-through correction under POL-RD-09(4), which costs the driver nothing and does not disturb the SGD 12.14 of distance and time fares this trip actually earned.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you should read this the same way: the distance and time charges for the ride stand, the SGD 2.00 CTE ERP line comes off, and SGD 2.00 is refunded to the rider.

What the trip shows. This is trip TRP-04006; the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry that identifier and agree on the timestamps. The platform's booked optimal route from Ang Mo Kio Ave 6 to Novena Medical Center was 8.7 km (EV-TRIP-04006). The governing distance is the GPS trace figure of 9.84 km (EV-GPS-04006), not the rounded 9.8 km convenience copy on the trip record, because POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern. Excess = 9.84 - 8.7 = 1.14 km, which is 13.1% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km. The 13.1% fails the percentage test, so no route deviation is established, however the morning felt and whatever a usual fare has been.

What follows for the contested amount. Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation is never reached, and the distance charge (9.84 km x SGD 0.75 = SGD 7.38) and time charge (17 min x SGD 0.28 = SGD 4.76) stand as billed. The ledger reconciles to the cent: 3.80 base + 7.38 + 4.76 + 2.00 ERP + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 18.74 charged.

The one line that cannot stand. The SGD 2.00 ERP charge for the CTE (southbound) gantry after Braddell Road, charged at 08:33, is for a gantry the trace never passes: the closest of the 104 fixes, at 08:34:30, is 1,843.93 m from the gantry's recorded coordinates, far outside the 250 m radius POL-RD-09(4) treats as a crossing. The booking route itemised ERP of SGD 0.00, and the fare block itself marks the line as off the optimal route (SGD 2.00 off-optimal against SGD 0.00 on-optimal). Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge for a gantry the trace never crosses is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists — and POL-RD-01 expressly preserves that limb where neither establishment test is met. Because no POL-RD-02 refund runs, nothing is double-counted (POL-RD-09(1)); and POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts a line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), so this case is ruled rather than held.

The accounts of both parties. The driver's statement that he went by Upper Thomson and Thomson Road and never used the CTE agrees with the planned corridor on the record (Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, Ave 1, Marymount Rd, Thomson Rd, Sinaran Dr) and with the trace, which never approaches the gantry; it is consistent with the ruling but is not what carries it. The rider's account of a loop round Yio Chu Kang and '4-5 km extra' is supported by no artifact in the bundle and is contradicted by the only measurement on file (1.14 km, not 4-5 km); under POL-RD-08 an assertion unsupported by evidence carries no weight. The driver's submission that the rider's claim be met with NO_ACTION is rejected so far as it would leave the ERP line in place: the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND on the rider's contested amount.

Points checked and not used as grounds. No traffic advisory exists in the bundle — EV-ADVIS-04006-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — but neither party asserts an external traffic cause or cites that identifier, so under POL-RD-13 there is nothing to test against it, POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable, and no POL-RD-10(5) escalation arises. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 104 fixes at a 10 s cadence, largest interval 10 s, largest straight-line step 114.0 m, highest implied speed 41.0 km/h. So the gap consequences of POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) do not engage, and the absence of any CTE crossing is a real absence rather than a hole in the record. POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not triggered, the deviation being neither established nor material, and consulted anyway it returns nothing: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 295 completed trips in 90 days, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The remaining profile fields mentioned on both sides (rating, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags, prior_disputes_filed) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground nothing here. POL-RD-04's compensation limb is not available: the billed distance (9.84 km) is not less than the trace distance, so there is no unbilled distance to pay for, and driver_compensation_sgd is null.

Amount and confidence. Contested SGD 6.00; refunded SGD 2.00, being the CTE ERP correction alone. Confidence is 0.9: the artifacts the ruling rests on — EV-GPS-04006, EV-TRIP-04006 and EV-FARE-04006 — all carry weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and the 0.70 floor is nowhere near. The monetary effect (SGD 2.00) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so under POL-GEN-05 it executes automatically on issue; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
